title: P300 dataset BI2015a from a "Brain Invaders" experiment
description: This dataset comprises electroencephalographic recordings from 43 healthy participants performing a visual P300-based brain-computer interface task using the Brain Invaders videogame paradigm. Participants completed three sessions with varying flash durations (50ms, 80ms, 110ms) while attempting to identify target symbols among 36 pseudo-randomly flashed stimuli. EEG data were acquired using 32 wet electrodes at 512 Hz, with real-time adaptive Riemannian classification providing online feedback without calibration. Resting state recordings (eyes closed, approximately one minute) were acquired before and after each session.
methods_description: EEG data were recorded from 43 healthy subjects (mean age 23.7±3.19 years; 31 male, 12 female) using 32 active wet electrodes in a 10-10 montage (g.GAMMAcap, g.tec) sampled at 512 Hz with g.USBamp hardware and OpenViBE software. The experiment employed an oddball paradigm with visual stimuli presented on a grid of 36 symbols (1 target, 35 non-targets) flashed pseudo-randomly at three flash durations across three game sessions. Reference electrode was placed at the right earlobe with ground at Fz. Resting state recordings (eyes closed, approximately one minute) were acquired before and after each session. Real-time adaptive Riemannian Minimum Distance to Mean classification provided visual feedback through the game interface.
